The Glasgow 1645 child 3971, Polwarth husband 3107 and Campbeltown father 1496 are also chronological possibilities. The inquest supplies no age, occupation or kin to distinguish them. Glasgow-3105 is a particularly relevant Kilwinning candidate. Its current biography explicitly withdraws 1670 as a documented birth: it is only an adult-status estimate from fatherhood in 1689. An older birth compatible with the 1674 adult inquest is permitted; remove the old too-young exclusion.

subject-old-monkland-thomson-sneddon-186.assessment: Mary Glasgon, wife of Robert Thomson and mother of the 1860 bride, remains compatible with the probate-defined Mary Thompson, Glasgow-4093, whose dates and husband’s forename are unknown. The Tannybrake widow’s reported age would conflict with this maternity, but that widow is an unproved candidate and cannot date or exclude Glasgow-4093. Scottish alternatives Glasgow-1351, Glasgow-1353, Glasgow-1453 and Glasgow-1531 have compatible adult chronology. Glasgow-1531 has a John Potts spouse without marriage boundaries that exclude a Robert Thomson marriage. None is established as this mother.

Thomson-3009 has an unsourced 1826 Barony birth, no spouse or death, and a sparse GEDCOM biography. Its tree parents are James Thomson-3008 and Helen Strathearn-36, conflicting with the index parents Robert Thomson and Mary Glasgon. Those imported fields and a death record for Annie with maternal surname Strathern do not directly establish Mary’s own parentage or prove full siblinghood. Thomson-3009 therefore remains a disputed candidate. Thomson-13010 has different parents Andrew Thomson and Elizabeth Waddell in a birth citation, and a recorded Abercrombie household; it is a specifically conflicting identity.

subject-old-monkland-thomson-sneddon-186.assessment: The complete 1,359-result search found Sneddon-710: William, age 30, coal miner at Huntlaw Colliery, Pencaitland in 1841, Scottish birth, spouse Mary Wilson and death unknown. Its difference from the marriage-derived 1815 needs comparison but is not a conclusive exclusion. Sneddon-756 is a father in 1823, which materially conflicts with the indexed 1815 birth range; Sneddon-765 was born in 1828. Sneddon-625’s verified 1820 birth also disagrees with age 45 in 1860.
